# Clarified specification for `executable`

The required artifact is one directly runnable program named exactly `executable`. It is a command-line page archiver compatible with Monolith 2.11.0: it accepts an HTML document, rewrites retrievable dependencies into the document, and emits one self-contained HTML or MHTML file. All behavior below is part of the executable unless a section explicitly describes input supplied by the operating system or test harness.

## Spec 1

The command-line shape is `executable [OPTIONS] <TARGET>`. Exactly one target is required. Options may precede or follow the target, long options accept `--name=value`, and compatible short boolean options may be combined (for example `-Ijci`, `-Mn`, and `-qi`). `--` ends option parsing, so the next token is the target even if it begins with `-`.

The supported options, with both spellings, are:

- `-a`, `--no-audio`
- `-b VALUE`, `--base-url VALUE`
- `-B`, `--blacklist-domains`
- `-c`, `--no-css`
- `-C FILE`, `--cookie-file FILE`
- repeatable `-d DOMAIN`, `--domain DOMAIN`
- `-e`, `--ignore-errors`
- `-E ENCODING`, `--encoding ENCODING`
- `-f`, `--no-frames`
- `-F`, `--no-fonts`
- `-i`, `--no-images`
- `-I`, `--isolate`
- `-j`, `--no-js`
- `-k`, `--insecure`
- `-m`, `--mhtml`
- `-M`, `--no-metadata`
- `-n`, `--unwrap-noscript`
- `-o FILE`, `--output FILE`
- `-q`, `--quiet`
- `-t INTEGER`, `--timeout INTEGER`
- `-u STRING`, `--user-agent STRING`
- `-v`, `--no-video`
- `-h`, `--help`
- `-V`, `--version`

Boolean flags take no value. A timeout is an unsigned decimal integer in seconds; zero and large values such as 999 are valid. User-agent, base URL, encoding, domain, cookie-file, and output options take exactly one value.

## Spec 2

`-V` and `--version` exit 0, write exactly `monolith 2.11.0\n` to standard output, and write nothing to standard error.

`-h` and `--help` exit 0, write nothing to standard error, end the output with a newline, and produce exactly the following text (the backslashes shown are literal):

## Spec 5 By default the completed archive is written to standard output. `-o -` explicitly selects standard output and behaves identically. A non-`-` output path is created or truncated and receives the complete result; stdout is then empty. An existing file is overwritten, not appended. Ordinary missing parent directories are not created. Failure to prepare the output path is a failure; compatibility with the reference includes the Rust-style exit status 101 and panic diagnostic for `/nonexistent/directory/output.html`, containing `thread 'main' (...) panicked at src/main.rs:` and `could not prepare output: Os { code: 2, kind: NotFound`. Before opening an output path, replace every occurrence of: - `%title%` with the document title text, or the empty string if no title exists; - `%ext%` with `htm` for HTML or `mht` for MHTML; - `%extension%` with `html` for HTML or `mhtml` for MHTML; - `%timestamp%` with the current UTC timestamp suitable for a filename. Multiple placeholders are all replaced. For filenames, sanitize a title colon as ` - `; thus title `Test: File & Data` used in `output-%title%.html` produces `output-Test - File & Data.html`. Other ordinary title characters, including spaces and `&`, remain. The title inside HTML retains its content and normal HTML escaping. ## Spec 6 Unless `-q` is set, each actual target or asset retrieval writes one line to standard error containing its normalized URL. Local paths are shown as absolute `file://` URLs. Retrieval errors append a parenthesized reason on the same line, such as `(file not found)`, `(is a directory)`, `(security error)`, `(builder error for url (...))`, an HTTP status, or `error sending request for url (...)`. Successful document content never goes to stderr. `-q` suppresses all such progress and run-time error messages, including fatal run-time diagnostics, without changing success/failure status or document bytes. It does not suppress help/version, parser diagnostics, or the archive when the archive itself is directed to stdout. `NO_COLOR` being set or `TERM=dumb` forces error diagnostics to contain no ANSI escape sequences; diagnostics captured through a non-TTY may also be uncolored. ## Spec 7 HTML input is parsed with forgiving HTML5 tree-building semantics and serialized deterministically. Missing `html`, `head`, or `body` elements are synthesized. Empty input becomes `...`. Malformed nesting and unclosed tags are repaired rather than rejected. Doctypes, comments, whitespace text, attributes, tables, forms, framesets, inline SVG, semantic HTML5 elements, and ordinary deep parent/child relationships are preserved. A `template` element is preserved, but its template contents are discarded: `` serializes as ``. Preservation of an HTML doctype means preserving its presence and parsed identity, not its source capitalization: an input `` is canonically serialized as exactly ``. Serialization uses lowercase HTML tag names, double-quoted attribute values, and normal HTML escaping. HTML void elements originating in input (`meta`, `link`, `img`, `input`, `br`, `hr`, `source`, and `frame`) have no slash and no end tag. Boolean attributes serialize with an empty value, for example `controls=""`. A generated robots, CSP, or custom-base node is serialized in the reference form with an explicit end tag (`` or ``), while a parsed pre-existing void element keeps ordinary void serialization. Preserve source whitespace and raw text as the HTML5 parser does, normalize CR/CRLF to LF in HTML, strip an initial UTF-8 BOM, and terminate processed HTML output with one LF. Text-only, one-character, whitespace-only, binary-contaminated, or null-containing input must still produce a document. Invalid byte sequences are replaced by U+FFFD under a UTF-8 decode. HTML entities are decoded into the DOM and safely re-escaped on serialization [TRUNCATED: full original retained on experiment server]
